research.topic: What a mental‑health screening test is (and what it cannot tell you)
verified: Screening tests measure symptom severity but do not provide a clinical diagnosis
They are intended for early identification of possible mental‑health issues, typically assessing symptoms over the past two weeks.
They are designed for early identification of possible mental‑health issues after symptoms persist for at least two weeks

sources.title: The PHQ-9: validity of a brief depression severity measure.
Validation and utility of a self-report version of PRIME-MD: the PHQ primary care study. Primary Care Evaluation of Mental Disorders. Patient Health Questionnai

research.hook: Kabhi aisa laga ki bas ek 5‑minute quiz se tum apni mental health ka ‘scorecard’ mil jayega?
research.tip: Set a weekly “mental‑check‑in”: spend 5 minutes completing a brief screen (e.g., PHQ‑2) and note the score; if it crosses the cutoff or you notice a sudden change, arrange a 15‑minute tele‑consultation within 48 hours.
dropped: Common screens like PHQ‑9 and GAD‑7 have been validated in diverse cultural populations, including S (unsupported)
Screening questionnaires are not intended to detect imminent risk of self‑harm or psychosis (unsupported)
Up to 15% of respondents may receive false‑positive or false‑negative scores (unsupported)
Repeating the same screen every 4‑6 weeks can track symptom change and guide help‑seeking (unsupported)

data.title: Mental Health Screening Ka Sach: Kya Bata Sakta Hai, Kya Nahi
data.title_en: What a Mental-Health Screening Test Really Shows

scenes.text: Kabhi laga quiz se sab pata chalega?
scenes.text_en: Ever thought a quiz could reveal everything?

scenes.text: Screening test sirf symptoms ki severity ko mapta hai—par kya yeh aapko madad karega?
scenes.text_en: A screening test only measures symptom severity—but can it help you?

scenes.text: Ye test 2 hafton ke symptoms ko assess karta hai.
scenes.text_en: It assesses symptoms over the past two weeks.

scenes.text: Engineering student Rohan, 2 hafton se low mood feel kar raha hai.
scenes.text_en: Engineering student Rohan has felt low mood for two weeks.

scenes.text: Ye koi clinical diagnosis nahi deta, doctor ki zaroorat hoti hai.
scenes.text_en: It doesn't give a clinical diagnosis; a doctor is needed.

scenes.text: Screening sirf severity batata hai, disease ka label nahi.
scenes.text_en: Screening only shows severity, not a disease label.

scenes.text: Early identification se help mil sakti hai, par treatment decide nahi.
scenes.text_en: Early identification can help, but it doesn't decide treatment.

scenes.text: Set karo weekly mental‑check‑in, 5 minute screen karo.
scenes.text_en: Set a weekly mental check‑in, do a 5‑minute screen.

scenes.text: Pehle PHQ‑2 ya similar test fill karo.
scenes.text_en: First, fill a PHQ‑2 or similar test.

scenes.text: Score ya change note karo; agar high ho to doctor ko call karo.
scenes.text_en: Note the score or change; if high, call a doctor.

scenes.text: 5‑minute PHQ‑2 karo; agar score 3 ya usse zyada ho, doctor ko book karo.
scenes.text_en: Take a 5‑minute PHQ‑2; if your score is 3 or higher, book a doctor.

data.description: A short reel explaining what mental‑health screening tests measure, what they cannot diagnose, and a simple weekly check‑in habit to stay proactive.

fixes: Reduce first line to ≤9 words for stronger hook
Add a concrete Indian student or professional example (e.g., engineering student, IT professional)
Make the final call‑to‑action explicit (e.g., ‘Take a 5‑minute PHQ‑2 today and book a doctor if score ≥3’)
Ensure open loop is introduced by scene 2 instead of scene 3
